text:
**My pick for most people: INIU SnapGo Air (10,000 mAh, Qi2.2 25 W).** It's about 0.5" thick and 195 g, so it's slim for a 10K bank. It charges an iPhone 17 wirelessly at 25 W, the fastest Qi2 speed, and does 45 W wired. It also has a built-in lanyard-style USB-C cable. Android Central lists it at $42.99 on Amazon ([Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge)). That article is where the Amazon and INIU buy links are. Macworld also calls it an "equal slimmest" 10K pick, but its list is limited to power banks it tested ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668978/feature-best-magsafe-magnetic-portable-battery-packs-power-banks-for-iphone.html)).

**If thinness matters most (5,000 mAh):**
- **Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim):** [buy at Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank). It's $54.99, 0.34" thick and 4.3 oz, with Qi2-certified 15 W wireless. Anker lists it as a best fit for the iPhone 17 series. 9to5Mac calls it the closest alternative to Apple's own MagSafe battery and says it runs cooler than the competition ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/)).
- **Baseus Picogo Air AM71:** Android Central found it the thinnest and lightest of its slim picks, at 0.27" and 104 g. The catch is that it only charges wirelessly at 7.5 W. It's listed at $52.99 at Amazon ([Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge)). I'd choose the Anker for the faster wireless speed.

**If you want more capacity and don't mind some bulk:**
- **Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10K, Qi2.2 25 W, 45 W wired):** $59.99, or $53.99 with code AM52 according to the listing. [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w). That page is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy through it. The checkout price is the final word.
- **UGREEN 10K Qi2.2:** about $59.99 on Amazon, but 9to5Mac notes it isn't as thin as the others ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/)). Macworld separately lists the UGREEN MagFlow Pro 10K as an equal-slimmest 10K with the best capacity test score.

**Things to know:**
- The iPhone 17 supports 25 W Qi2.2, but only the 10K models above reach it. The 5K slim ones top out at 15 W or less.
- A 5K bank typically recharges a phone about 60–75% of the way. A 10K bank can charge it close to twice.
- Thick or non-magnetic cases can weaken the connection. Anker says cases over 2.5 mm may interfere.
- Prices change often, so check the checkout page.

If you tell me whether you'd rather have the thinnest option or enough capacity for a full day, I can narrow it to one.
